title: CPU, GPU, Memory, and Storage
summary: Compare processing, working memory, and storage choices for different computing work.
objectives: Distinguish CPU, GPU, RAM, and storage roles.
Compare HDD, SSD, and NVMe at a conceptual level.

vocab.def: A general-purpose processor that carries out many kinds of instructions.
A processor designed for many parallel calculations, useful for graphics and some AI workloads.
Temporary working memory used while programs are running.
Solid-state storage with no spinning disk.

sections.heading: Processing is not storage
sections.body: The CPU handles general-purpose instructions. A GPU can handle many similar calculations in parallel, which can help graphics and some AI workloads. Neither one replaces RAM or storage.

sections.heading: Working memory and long-term storage
sections.body: RAM is fast working space and is usually temporary when power is removed. HDDs use spinning disks, while SSDs and NVMe devices use solid-state storage. Capacity, speed, cost, and reliability all matter.

sections.heading: Safe comparison lab
sections.body: Use a synthetic hardware table to compare components. Do not remove drives, open power supplies, or alter a real server. The lab is about interpreting specifications, not hardware repair.

practice.prompt: A workload needs many parallel calculations and fast working data. Which components would you compare first, and what tradeoff might remain?

quiz.question: What is RAM mainly used for?
options: Temporary working information while programs run
quiz.answer: Temporary working information while programs run

lab.objective: Interpret a synthetic component specification table.

reflectionPrompt: Which specification would matter most for a workload you use, and why?
